column3: Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
“Said” renders the Greek present “says”; “more” is not separately stated after their having no wine.
The Greek idiom directly names “Me and you”; BSB renders it as “us.”
“Said” renders present “says.”
The Greek gives two or three metretae, while BSB converts the quantity to gallons.
“The servants” makes the pronoun explicit; “told” renders present “says.”
The Greek explicitly says they carried it, rather than the general “did so,” and uses present “says.”
“Aside” is supplied; “called” renders present “calls.”
The Greek says inferior wine rather than explicitly cheap wine; “the guests” supplies the unnamed subject.
The Greek calls this the beginning of the signs; “thus” makes the connection explicit.
The Greek says “not many days,” rather than the positive “a few days.”
Close to the Greek.
“Courts” and “at their tables” are supplied.
“Courts” and the possessive “their” before tables are supplied.
The Greek prohibits making the house a house of trade; BSB adds the rhetorical form “How dare you.”
Close to the Greek.
“To prove Your authority” explains the Greek connection “that You do these things.”
“Again” is supplied.
Close to the Greek.
“Jesus” supplies the Greek pronoun’s referent.
Close to the Greek.
BSB moves seeing the signs before believing, while the Greek places belief first with a participle of seeing.
Close to the Greek.
The Greek explicitly describes someone bearing testimony; BSB compresses this to “any testimony.”
